title: ĐẶC ĐIỂM HÌNH ẢNH VÀ BIẾN THỂ MẠCH MÁU VÙNG MẠC TREO TỤY TRÊN CẮT LỚP VI TÍNH ĐA DÃY: NGHIÊN CỨU MÔ TẢ HỒI CỨU TẠI BỆNH VIỆN BẠCH MAI
journal: Vietnamese Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine
abstract: Mạc treo là vùng mô liên kết - thần kinh - mạch máu nằm phía sau đầu tổn thương và mím móc vá, có liên quan đến đường lan tràn của bệnh lý ác tính vùng đầu sẹo và chiến lược lướt thuật cắt khối tá tụy. Nhận được hình ảnh đặc biệt và các mạch máu biến đổi trong vùng này có ý nghĩa trong đánh giá tiền cảnh. Mục tiêu: Mô tả đặc điểm hình thái, các hình ảnh thông số và phân chia mạch máu vùng võng mạc treo trên cắt lớp vi tính đa chuỗi kết hợp dựng hình ba chiều. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang hồi nghiên cứu trên 129 trường hợp hợp được chụp CLVT đa chuỗi truyền máu tiêm quang tại Bệnh viện Bạch Mai từ tháng 10/2025 đến tháng 5/2026. Hình ảnh được phân tích trên hệ thống PACS và phần mềm Syngo.Thông qua việc đánh giá thái độ, thể tích, tỷ lệ, kích thước và cấu trúc mạch máu trong vùng diều sâu. Kết quả: Tuổi trung bình của nhóm nghiên cứu là 52 ± 18 tuổi. Mạc treo thiếu chủ yếu có hình chuông (51,94%) hoặc đa diện (48,06%). Thể tích trung bình là 6,48 ± 4,44 cm³; tỷ lệ trung bình là -12,64 ± 29,39 HU. Mạch máu trong vùng tổn thương của võng mạc được nhận diện ở 99,22% trường hợp. IPDA và IPDV là hai cấu trúc thường gặp nhất, lần lượt sử dụng 95,35% và 86,82%. IPDA thường phân tách chung với nhánh hỗ trợ mạch tràng đầu tiên (61,79%), trong khi IPDV thường chuyển về mạch hỗ trợ mạch mạch đầu tiên (55,35%). Kết luận: CLVT kết hợp nhiều chuỗi theo ba chiều cho phép nhận dạng hình ảnh cụ thể và các mạch máu của vùng diều sâu. IPDA và IPDV là các giải pháp thông minh, có giá trị định hướng trong việc đánh giá tiền bảo vệ vùng đầu đục.

title: Why are farmers in South India shifting from conventional ‘Green Revolution’ agriculture to natural farming?
abstract: Introduction The Green Revolution contributed to significant increases in crop production and yield in India. However, it also resulted in negative social and environmental consequences. In response, alternative farming practices have emerged, based on agroecological principles, such as natural farming. In recent years, government policies at state and national levels have promoted natural farming. However, anecdotal evidence suggests its adoption by farmers has been limited and uneven. The aim of this study was to understand barriers and facilitators involved in transitioning to natural farming in India in the context of a government natural farming program at the early stages of implementation. Methods An exploratory sequential mixed methods design was used. Eleven focus group discussions (FGDs) were conducted in six villages across Anakapalli and Visakhapatnam districts of Andhra Pradesh from March to May 2023. FGD transcripts were coded and analyzed using a constant comparative method. Subsequently, a questionnaire was developed based on the FGD findings and administered to heads of 1,126 households across 82 villages in four districts in Andhra Pradesh from October to November 2023. Qualitative and quantitative findings were analyzed separately and subsequently integrated using the ‘Diffusion of Innovations’ theory. Results Adoption rates of natural farming were low after the first few months of training, with just 23 out of 1,126 households adopting any natural farming practices. Farmers perceived that health benefits were a relative advantage of adopting natural farming over conventional farming. Internal community resource persons (iCRPs) and presentations on a Pico projector (i.e., handheld projector)emerged as predominant channels of communication. Preexisting institutional architecture in the form of women’s self-help groups contributed to an enabling social system. However, a lack of decentralized input supply, weak market linkages, perceived yield penalties and the labor- and knowledge-intensive nature of natural farming were key barriers. Conclusion The study highlights the importance of understanding the diverse motivations of farmers to adopt natural farming. Modeling peer-to-peer learning, use of mass media, and decentralized input supply may lead to improvement in natural farming uptake. Tailoring policies to address specific needs of conventional and natural farmers will likely facilitate a smoother transition to natural farming.

title: Who bears the burden of monetary tightening? credit default responses across income groups and firm sizes in Brazil
abstract: Abstract This paper examines heterogeneous monetary transmission to credit default in Brazil, exploiting granular disaggregation by income bracket, firm size, and state. Using monthly Central Bank data from 2012 to 2024 covering all 27 Brazilian states, we document heterogeneous predictive responses across households and firms. In the baseline Selic-path estimates, household responses are strongest in the middle of the income distribution, particularly across the 1–5 minimum-wage brackets, while responses at higher incomes are smaller; this household ordering is not recovered with comparable precision in the exercise based on unexpected Selic target changes. On the corporate side, small firms display the clearest baseline responses, emerging after roughly 10–14 months, while micro firms also react but with less precise aggregate baseline evidence. The surprise-based exercise provides clearer support on the firm side, and additional sectoral and product-level results point to institutional credit segmentation, with free and short-term corporate credit responding more strongly than more protected categories. Overall, the evidence is strongest for firm-side heterogeneity, while the household pattern is best interpreted as a suggestive reduced-form result of the baseline analysis.

title: When market orientation backfires: the asymmetric effects of proactive and responsive orientation on marketing capabilities and performance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how proactive and responsive market orientations (RMOs) are associated with the development of digital and traditional marketing capabilities (TMCs) in business-to-business (B2B) small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and how those capabilities are related to multiple performance outcomes. It also considers whether misalignment between strategic orientation and capability development may constrain performance. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 300 managerial respondents with knowledge of marketing and sales activities in South Korean B2B SMEs, with substantial representation from manufacturing and related sectors. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the relationships among proactive and RMO, digital marketing capabilities (DMCs), TMCs and digital innovation, cost reduction, sales and customer performance. Findings The results reveal a clear asymmetry: proactive market orientation is positively associated with both DMCs and TMCs, whereas RMO is negatively associated with both capabilities. This pattern suggests that an excessive focus on expressed customer needs may be related to more limited capability development. DMCs are positively associated with digital innovation performance, cost reduction and sales performance, but are not significantly related to customer performance. TMCs are positively associated with both sales and customer performance. Overall, the findings suggest that digital transformation outcomes are related to the alignment between strategic orientation and capability development. Originality/value This study identifies specialized marketing capabilities as a critical link between market orientation (MO) and performance and documents the asymmetric, potentially limiting role of RMO. It challenges the assumption that all forms of MO are uniformly beneficial and offers a context-sensitive reinterpretation of how strategic orientations are related to capability development in digital transformation settings.

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence to Identify Invisible Barriers in Inclusive Education: An Exploratory Bibliographic Review (2020-2026)
abstract: The study concludes that AI should not replace educational listening, but it can support the identification of less visible inequalities and strengthen policies for student retention, accessibility, and educational justice.

title: Trade integration in digitally enabled economies: implications for brand scalability in the EU27
journal: European Journal of Management and Business Economics
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital transformation tools, specifically artificial intelligence (AI), big data, social media and cloud computing, relate to countries' globalisation degree across the EU27. Adopting a macro-structural perspective, it investigates how national digital infrastructure shapes trade integration and, in turn, the structural conditions under which brand scalability becomes possible in international markets. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on harmonised secondary data from DESI, the World Bank, and the Observatory of Economic Complexity. A globalisation degree indicator based on trade intensity is constructed and analysed using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression models. The analysis examines the associations between digital capabilities and globalisation degree, while accounting for economic (GDP) and demographic (population size) moderators. Additional models explore the enabling roles of big data and cloud computing in relation to AI and social media at the structural level. Findings The results indicate that artificial intelligence is most strongly associated with globalisation degree across the EU27. Big data and cloud computing are not directly associated with globalisation degree in the main model but show consistent enabling relationships in auxiliary analyses. Social media exhibits a weak and negative association at the macro-structural level. These findings suggest a layered digital configuration in which integrative digital capabilities are more closely linked to trade-based market integration than engagement-oriented tools. The association between AI and globalisation degree is also context-dependent, being stronger in digitally mature and trade-active environments. Originality/value This study contributes to international marketing and digital branding research by reframing global branding as a structurally conditioned process at the macro-level, rather than a purely firm-driven one. By empirically modelling the macro-level digital antecedents of trade integration, it clarifies where digital transformation exerts its influence and establishes a foundation for future multi-level research on brand scalability in global markets.

title: Tourism development of UNESCO world heritage sites: a comparative analysis of sustainable strategies between Italy and Saudi Arabia
journal: Journal of Cultural Heritage Management and Sustainable Development
abstract: Purpose The research aims to explore strategies adopted for the sustainable management of heritage tourism through a comparative analysis of the sites of Pompeii (Italy) and Al Ula (Saudi Arabia). Design/methodology/approach The study employs a qualitative comparative case study approach, triangulating data from official management plans and sustainability reports with empirical on-site observations conducted between 2023 and 2024 to ensure data validity and reliability. Findings The results highlight contrasting approaches: Pompeii is more focused on heritage conservation, while Al Ula has a holistic approach geared toward site development. While Al Ula considers the three aspects of sustainability, Pompeii lacks environmental sustainability policies. Furthermore, while Al Ula’s primary needs concern heritage conservation, economic vitality, social engagement and environmental performance, Pompeii focuses primarily on heritage conservation, infrastructure and services, community engagement, and environmental performance. Originality/value The research’s originality lies in identifying crucial aspects at both sites essential for the sustainable management of tourism in heritage sites, including value, community engagement, green infrastructure, economic growth and social impact.

title: The transcription factor UvCreA regulates ustilaginoidin synthesis and pathogenicity in Ustilaginoidea virens
abstract: Abstract Ustilaginoidea virens produces several types of mycotoxins, including ustilaginoidins, during infection. The transcription factor CreA plays a central role in carbon catabolite repression, coordinating carbon source utilization during fungal growth, development, and host infection. However, knowledge is limited regarding the specific functions and molecular mechanisms by which CreA regulates mycotoxin biosynthesis and pathogenicity. In this study, we found that the wild-type U. virens strain exhibited significantly different ustilaginoidin-producing capacities under distinct carbon sources. The UvCreA gene knockout mutants exhibited slower mycelial growth, reduced pathogenicity and ustilaginoidin production, but produced significantly more conidiospores than the wild type. Consistently, expression of ustilaginoidin biosynthetic genes was significantly downregulated in the UvCreA mutant. Moreover, yeast one-hybrid and electrophoretic mobility shift assays confirmed that UvCreA binds to the promoters of the polyketide synthase gene UvPKS1 and the methyltransferase gene UgsJ . ChIP-qPCR showed significant enrichment in promoter regions of UvPKS1 and UgsJ . These findings indicate that UvCreA not only controls ustilaginoidin biosynthesis through directly binding the Ugs gene promoters, but also positively regulates mycelial growth and pathogenicity in U. virens . Therefore, this study provides theoretical insights into the regulatory mechanism of mycotoxin biosynthesis in phytopathogenic fungi.

title: Public service motivation in fragile contexts: the mediating power of remote e-working in Lebanon's NGO sector
journal: International Journal of Organization Theory & Behavior
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how public service motivation (PSM) influences employee performance in nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) operating under fragility and examines whether remote e-working (REW) mediates this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 226 employees working in local and international NGOs in Lebanon. Structural equation modeling with partial least squares was used to test the hypothesized mediation model. Findings REW partially mediates the relationship between PSM and employee performance. Remote arrangements appear to translate prosocial motives into higher performance by enhancing autonomy, flexibility and technology-enabled engagement. Practical implications NGO leaders and policymakers should design remote work systems that support autonomy, trust, clear objectives and reliable digital tools. Investment in training, performance feedback and secure platforms can help sustain performance in challenging contexts. Originality/value The study integrates PSM with emerging evidence on flexible work to explain performance mechanisms in fragile environments, showing how REW operates as a pathway from motivation to outcomes.
